limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).
Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.
DeckCheck's Threat Index is shown in `context` and never scored.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.
rank over n=5 decks; no significance claim

open_questions.question: Does the sacrifice engine get cast and used by Forge's AI? A cast check on this list is needed; diagnosis should name it as the unproven link.

findings.note: 62 sits 4 under code_score but the cited record argues lower. Meren's kill_by_turn_8 is 0.268 against 0.464-0.774 for the other four decks in rank.group, and never_kills_rate is 0.187. Median kill is turn 9 (tied last with emiel-blink, 48.5). The table-wide drain is drawn by turn six in only 34% of games and the core trio in 11%. The pilot's own bar (context:pilot) is 'lethal, consistent and fast'. goblin-storm (63.0) kills by turn 8 in 0.565 of games, yet this judgment lands within a point of it. 'Do not deduct again' for speed is stated but not shown to be correct: speed's 0.2 weight_effective is the only place slowness enters, and the trio figure is a separate assembly shortfall.

'many games will find the trio after [the median kill]' is not in the record. context:numbers gives the trio only by turn six (11%); there is no by-turn-nine figure. The argument turns this guess into 'a limit on a mid-game threat rather than proof the deck fails to assemble'. 'The supply of parts is good' also skips the 34% table-wide drain and the 6% Starscape multiplier that the context lists.

'The pilot's no-two-card-infinites rule also gives up the fastest lines on purpose' ranks lines by speed without enumerating them. combos.json shows 5 known lines, all infinite, 0 two-card, and the record does not say which is fastest or what they would have added.

The question is whether Forge's AI casts the sacrifice engine. settled_by 'diagnose' cannot answer it, because diagnose runs no Forge game. The charter's own answerer is forge-cast-check. No engine.json exists yet, so diagnose has no engine stage to read.
Median turn 9 matches the context numbers block, and benchmark.json agrees (median_kill_turn 9).
92%, 74%, 51%, 80% and 11% are verbatim in the CONTEXT.md numbers block, written for sha 7da890b95460, which matches the decklist.
'no two-card infinites, ever' is verbatim in the CONTEXT.md pilot section (line 108).

Each strategy quote is verbatim and read in context. The 26% turn-3 miss belongs to Roach's average EDHREC deck, which is fine as a benchmark. The power-level quote is about expected game length across brackets, which is the claim made. components, withheld, code_score, bracket and limits are identical on re-run (validate-rating OK).

resolution: the interval spans 1 grade boundary (65); measured components carry their inputs' intervals, the judgment none

judgment.argument: The measured components cannot see a played deck: no games, no survey, no Forge run are withheld and their weight is redistributed, and there is no engine.json or stack. What I fill in is the shape of the engine from the goldfish context. Speed (26.8) already carries the slowness, since the goldfish median kill is turn 9 against an unopposed table, so I do not deduct for it again. The pieces are there: the commander is cast by turn six in 92% of games, recurring fodder is drawn by turn six in 74%, a free sacrifice outlet in 51%, and removal in 80%. The one soft spot is the full trio of outlet, table-wide drain and fodder: only 11% of games have drawn all three by turn six. That is a by-turn-six figure, and since the median kill comes later, many games will find the trio after it, so I read it as a limit on a mid-game threat rather than proof the deck fails to assemble. The pilot's no-two-card-infinites rule also gives up the fastest lines on purpose. Nothing has been played, which keeps me from lifting it far. I sit slightly under the 66.2 the components give: the supply of parts is good, the early assembly is thin, and neither has met a table.
